newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital beer drinkers to go metric.
newsitem.headline: China capital beer drinkers to go metric.

text.p: China's growing army of beer drinkers in Beijing will have to drink their tipple in litres from next year when the city government bans the traditional "zha" -- or mug -- in favour of metric measures.

The Beijing Technology Supervision Bureau would forbid restaurants and bars from using the word "zha", a slang term meaning a mug of draught beer, because the word was not an internationally accepted unit of volume, a bureau official said by telephone.

"From January 1, 1997, the only volume standard in selling unpackaged beer will be a litre. If customers want to buy a beer in restaurants or hotels, they should ask for 'one litre' or a 'half-litre'," the official said.
The move toward standardisation will mean all beer glasses in the city would have to be replaced with mugs showing a litre graduation and displaying a product label of the country of origin, he said.
